walkthroughs.body_html:
Genetics, Evolution & Ecosystems — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Genetics, Evolution & Ecosystems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Genetics, Evolution & Ecosystems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Approximate energy transfer between consumer trophic levels is:
Eutrophication leads to fish kills mainly because of:
options: Toxic algae
Reduced dissolved oxygen
Excess sunlight
Low temperatures
Mutations occur because organisms need to adapt to their environment.
They are random changes in DNA — caused by errors in replication or by mutagens — not directed by need.
Mutations only happen in organisms that have been damaged by external chemicals.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.

mcqs.q: How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Mutations only happen in organisms that have been damaged by external chemicals.
Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Mutations only happen in organisms that have been damaged by external chemicals.
Humans evolved directly from chimpanzees, which is why chimps still exist as a less-evolved version.
Humans evolved from monkeys but chimps evolved from gorillas.
No — humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor; both have evolved from it.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Trophic level”?
options: Cycling of nitrogen via fixation (Rhizobium), nitrification (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter), denitrification and decomposition.
A feeding level within an ecosystem; producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, etc.
Autotroph that converts light or chemical energy into biomass; e.g. plants, algae.
Energy passed to next trophic level as a percentage; about 10% between consumers, lower for producers.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Energy transfer efficiency”?
options: NPP = GPP − R, energy available to next trophic level after respiratory losses.
Enrichment of waters with nutrients causing algal blooms, decomposition by bacteria and O₂ depletion.
A feeding level within an ecosystem; producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers, etc.
